summary: Eduard Müller was an Indologist and linguist specializing in Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Leipzig (~1873-1874) and under Ernst Kuhn (~1874-1876). He served as professor at the University of Bern (~1886-1908).

Linguist Eduard Prokosch studied at Charles University, Vienna, Chicago (M.A.), and Leipzig (Ph.D.). He taught at Wisconsin-Madison (1905-1913), Texas at Austin as professor of German (1913-1919), Bryn Mawr (1919-1928), and Yale as Sterling Professor of Germanic Languages (1929).

Eduard Röer worked in Indology and philosophy, studying at Jena, Königsberg, and Berlin (Ph.D.) under Franz Bopp and J. F. Herbart. He taught at Berlin (1833-1838) and served as Asiatic Society librarian (~1841-1861) and Bibliotheca Indica editor (1848-1861).

Eduard Sachau was a linguist and scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies. Educated at Kiel, Leipzig, and Halle (Ph.D.), he taught at Vienna (1869), Berlin (from 1876), and directed the Seminar für Orientalische Sprachen (1887).

Eduard Schwyzer was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Zurich (Ph.D. under Adolf Kaegi) and Leipzig. He held professorships at the University of Zurich (from 1909), the University of Bonn (1927), and Humboldt University of Berlin (1932-1939).

Eduard Sievers, a linguist, completed his doctorate at Leipzig under Friedrich Zarncke and Georg Curtius. He held professorships at the University of Jena (1871-1883), Tübingen (1883-1887), Halle (1887-1892), and Leipzig (1892-1922).
Eduard Thommen was an Indologist who studied at the University of Basel (~1898-1902) under Jacob Wackernagel, Paris, Oxford, and completed his PhD at the University of Göttingen (~1902-1903).

Linguist Eduard Wölfflin studied at the University of Basel (~1849-1851) and the University of Göttingen (~1851-1854). He later held academic posts at the universities of Zurich (~1861-1869), Erlangen-Nuremberg (~1869-1880), and Munich (~1880-1905).

Eduard Zeller was a scholar of philosophy and religious studies who studied at the University of Tübingen (~1831-1836). He held posts at Tübingen (~1840-1847), Bern (~1847-1849), Marburg (~1849-1862), Heidelberg (~1862-1872), and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1872-1895).

Eduardo Francisco Freyre Roach is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Buddhist Studies at the University of Hong Kong (attested 2014), supervised by Yakupitiyage Karunadasa and Georgios T. Halkias.
Eduardo Luigi De Stefani was a scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied under Paolo Emilio Pavolini. In 1910, he held a teaching post in Latin and Greek grammar at Sapienza University of Rome.
Edvard Brandes was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at the University of Copenhagen under Niels Ludvig Westergaard, earning an M.A. in Oriental Philology (~1865-1872) and a Ph.D. (~1872-1879).

Edvard Westermarck worked in philosophy and religious studies. After studying at the University of Helsinki (~1881-1890), he held posts at the London School of Economics (~1904-1930) and Åbo Akademi University (~1918-1932).
Edward Albert Gait was an Indologist and historian who studied at University College London (~1880-1882). He founded the Bihar Research Society in 1914 and served as its president from 1915 to 1920.

Edward Amundsen worked in tibetology and linguistics. He served with the Tibetan Pioneer Mission (1893), the British and Foreign Bible Society as Superintendent for South-West China and Tibet (1903-1915), and Det Norske Misjonsforbund (1919-1924).

Edward Arthur Henry Blunt worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Corpus Christi College, Oxford (B.A.), and University College London. He joined the Indian Civil Service (1901) and became Financial Secretary for Uttar Pradesh (1920-1935).

Edward Backhouse Eastwick was a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies educated at Oxford. He served as professor of Hindustani and Telugu (1845) and librarian (1850) at East India Company College, later joining the Foreign Office.

Edward Byles Cowell was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Horace Hayman Wilson at Magdalen Hall. He served as principal of Sanskrit College (1858-1864) and professor of Sanskrit at the University of Cambridge from 1867 to 1903.

Edward C. Dimock Jr. was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Yale and Harvard (Ph.D. under Daniel H. H. Ingalls). He taught at the University of Chicago (1959-1993) and served as president of the American Institute of Indian Studies.

Edward Capps was a scholar of history, archaeology, and linguistics who studied at Illinois College, Yale, Berlin, Halle, and Munich. He held faculty posts at Illinois College (1887-1888), Yale University (1890-1907), and Princeton University (1907-1936).
